{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
{{BLP primary sources|date=February 2021}}[[File:Roland-wiesendanger.jpg|thumb|Roland Wiesendanger during the awarding of the Julius Springer Prize 2016]]
'''Roland Wiesendanger''' (born 5 October 1961 in [[Basel]]) is a German physicist, specializing in [[nanoscience]]. Since 1993 he has been a full professor at the [[University of Hamburg]], Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physik.uni-hamburg.de/inf/ag-wiesendanger/team/wiesendanger-roland.html |title=Prof. Dr. Roland Wiesendanger: Nanostruktur- und Festkörperphysik: Universität Hamburg |website=physik.uni-hamburg.de |access-date=21 April 2022 |language=German}}</ref>

He has been awarded three times in a row with the [[ERC Advanced Grant]] of the [[European Research Council]] as first scientist in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uni-hamburg.de/newsroom/presse/2018/pm23.html |title=2,5 Millionen Euro für neue Quantencomputer-Konzepte: Physikprofessor der Universität Hamburg zum dritten Mal bei europäischem Exzellenz-Wettbewerb erfolgreich|website=uni-hamburg.de |date= 1 April 2018 |language=German}}</ref>

== Early life and education==
According to the CV published on his department website, Wiesendanger was born in [[Basel]].<ref name="cv">{{Cite web |date=n.d. |title=CV of Prof. Dr. Dr. h.c. Roland Wiesendanger |url=http://www.nanoscience.de/HTML/PDF/CV_Wiesendanger_english.pdf |website=nanoscience.de}}</ref>

He grew up in [[Lörrach]], Germany, where he attended high-school, the [[Hans-Thoma-Gymnasium]] from 1972{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}  to 1981.<ref name="cv" /> He started studying physics, mathematics, and astronomy{{citation needed|date=November 2019}} at the [[University of Basel]], Switzerland in 1981.<ref name="cv" /> Since 1984 he had been working in the field of [[scanning tunneling microscopy]].{{citation needed|date=November 2019}} In 1986, he graduated in physics with highest distinction<ref name="cv" /> and in 1987, he received his PhD with "summa cum laude" in [[experimental physics]]<ref name="cv" /> for his work on "Scanning Tunneling Microscopy on Non-Crystalline Solids".{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}

==Career==
Until his Habilitation degree in 1990, he set up a unique Surface Science Instrument ("NANOLAB-I") which allowed for the simultaneous investigation of the structure, electronic and magnetic properties of surfaces at the atomic scale.{{citation needed|date=November 2019}}

In 1992 Wiesendanger received an offer for a [[full professor]] position for Experimental Physics at the [[University of Hamburg]], connected with the Foundation of the Microstructure Advanced Research Center Hamburg. 
He established a National Center of Competence in Nanotechnology.{{citation needed|date=October 2021}}

==Work==
Wiesendanger is author or co-author of more than 600 scientific publications as well as several books.

In February 2021, he released a working paper and preprint, non-peer-reviewed publication suggesting that [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] had [[COVID-19 lab leak theory|escaped from a lab in Wuhan]], a story which was picked up by many German news services including TV.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ndr.de/nachrichten/hamburg/Hamburger-Forscher-Coronavirus-stammt-wohl-aus-Labor,corona6764.html|title=Hamburger Forscher: Coronavirus stammt wohl aus Labor|work=[[Norddeutscher Rundfunk]]|language=de|date=18 February 2021}}</ref> Wiesendanger himself does not see his "study" as a formal scientific publication, but it "is intended to serve as information for a broad public in Germany".<ref>Lars Wienand: [https://www.t-online.de/nachrichten/deutschland/id_89506466/umstrittene-corona-studie-prof-wiesendanger-wuhan-und-die-biowaffen-.html ''Der Physikprofessor, Wuhan und die Biowaffen.''] Telefoninterview T-Online, 20. Februar 2021.</ref>

==Memberships and service==
Since 2000 Wiesendanger is a member of the [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|National Academy Leopoldina]], since 2005 member of the [[Academy of Sciences in Hamburg]], and since 2008 member of the [[acatech|German Academy of Science and Engineering]] (acatech). In 2012 he became Honorary Professor of the [[Harbin Institute of Technology]] (China) and in 2015 he received an Honorary Doctor degree from the [[Poznań University of Technology]] (Poland).

He has organized numerous international conferences like the International Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM’97) Conference in Hamburg (1997) or the 1st Otto Stern Symposium in Hamburg (2013). He has been a speaker at more than 500 international conferences, workshops and colloquia worldwide.

* 2013: Foreign Member of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[http://scienceinpoland.pap.pl/en/news/news%2C405669%2Cprof-roland-wiesendanger-received-an-honorary-doctorate-from-poznan-university-of-technology.html ''Prof. Roland Wiesendanger received an honorary doctorate from Poznań University of Technology.''] Press release on scienceinpoland.pap.pl. retrieved on 26 August 2019.</ref>

* 2015: International Fellow of the [[Surface Science Society of Japan]]

* 2018: 3rd ERC Advanced Grant<ref>[https://www.uni-hamburg.de/newsroom/presse/2018/pm23.html ''Physikprofessor der Universität Hamburg zum dritten Mal bei europäischem Exzellenz-Wettbewerb erfolgreich.''] Press release of the University of Hamburg. retrieved on 26 August 2019.</ref>
* 2019: [[Honorary Medal]] „De Scientia et Humanitate Optime Meritis" of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]]<ref>[https://www.min.uni-hamburg.de/ueber-die-fakultaet/aktuelles/2019/0521-honorary-medal-an-roland-wiesendanger-verliehen.html ''Honorary Medal an Roland Wiesendanger verliehen.''] Press release of the University of Hamburg. retrieved on 26 August 2019.</ref>
